# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 9 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 9
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. The circumcision they put their trust in — what does he say about it? "This is what the Lord your God says" — and here I find a brand-new commandment — "Do not plant among thorns; be circumcised to the Lord your God."
2. And further: "Circumcise the hard callus around your hearts, and stop stiffening your necks." And again: "Look," says the Lord, "every nation is uncircumcised in the flesh, but this people is uncircumcised in the heart."
3. You might say: but the people did receive circumcision as a sign! Yes — but so has every Syrian, every Arab, every idol priest. Are they part of the covenant then? The Egyptians are circumcised too!
4. So learn this thoroughly, beloved children: Abraham was the first to perform circumcision. He did it with his eyes on Jesus, guided by the Spirit, and he received in it the meaning of three letters.
5. Scripture says: "Abraham circumcised eighteen and three hundred men from his household." What knowledge was hidden in that number? Notice: the eighteen comes first, then — after a pause in the text — the three hundred.
6. Eighteen: I (iota) = 10, H (eta) = 8. Put them together: IH — that is "Jesus." And because the cross in the shape of T (tau) was destined to convey grace, the text adds "three hundred" [tau = 300]. So the two letters point to Jesus; the single letter points to the cross.
7. Only the one who implanted his teaching in us truly knows this. I have given you no word more true than this — and I know you are ready for it.
